page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-144-lssd is a memory-optimized server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 144 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 72 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system operates at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz and includes a substantial 504 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 1116 GB of RAM, providing approximately 7.75 GB of memory per vCPU.

This instance includes bundled local storage consisting of 24 NVMe SSDs, totaling 9383 GB of high-speed local capacity. While it does not feature any dedicated GPUs, the Intel Xeon processor integrates Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512), which accelerate matrix multiplication and vector operations directly on the CPU.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores all placing in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, achieving top-tier read and write speeds. The instance also excels in database operations, with Redis SET operations reaching 219.47 million operations per second. However, single-core performance is moderate, falling into the middle 50% for stress-ng single-core tests.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-highmem-144-lssd offers high resource density, combining massive memory capacity with extensive local NVMe storage. This makes it highly suitable for large-scale database deployments, in-memory caching layers, multi-threaded data processing, and CPU-based LLM prompt processing.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-144-lssd is a high-density, memory-optimized server configured with 144 dedicated vCPUs across 72 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor. Operating at 2.3 GHz, the system features 1116 GB of RAM and 9383 GB of local NVMe SSD storage across 24 drives. While lacking dedicated GPUs, the CPU supports Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 for hardware-accelerated vector and matrix operations. Benchmarks show top-tier multi-core CPU performance, exceptional memory bandwidth, and superior database throughput, although single-core performance remains average. This instance is highly suited for large-scale databases, high-throughput Redis caching, and memory-intensive enterprise workloads.
